For we see that if they are thrown into the **Fire**, the **Aqueous Spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum Aqueum"; the watery vapor or essence contained within a mineral.</note> breaks out with a loud noise before a **Flame** is conceived. This also happens gently in leaves that are somewhat more stubborn, the watery part breaking out before the oily part catches **Flame**. But this is most clearly seen in **Quicksilver** <note>original: "Argento vivo"</note>, which is not wrongly called **Mineral Water**. For this substance, without catching fire, almost equals the power of **Gunpowder** <note>original: "Pulvis Pyrius"</note> through simple **Eruption** and **Expansion**; it is also said that when mixed with **Gunpowder**, it multiplies its strength.

Similarly, let the <term>Natura Inquisita</term> <gloss>Nature under investigation</gloss> be the transitory nature of **Flame** and its momentary extinction. For it does not seem that the **Flaming Nature** is fixed or remains stable here with us, but is generated at almost every single moment and immediately extinguished. It is evident that in **Flames** which continue and endure here, that duration is not of the same **Flame** in the <term>Individuo</term> <gloss>individual instance</gloss>, but occurs through a succession of new **Flames** generated in a series; the same numerical **Flame** does not remain at all. This is easily perceived from the fact that once the nourishment or **fuel** <note>original: "fomite"</note> of the **Flame** is withdrawn, the **Flame** immediately perishes. There is a <term>Bivium</term> <gloss>fork in the road; a crucial crossroad</gloss> regarding this nature, as follows. This momentary nature either happens because the **Cause** which first generated it ceases, as in **Light** <note>original: "Lumen"</note>, **Sounds**, and so-called violent **Motions**; or because **Flame** could, by its own nature, remain here with us, but from a con

<summary>Bacon compares the explosive expansion of mercury and salts to gunpowder and observes that flame is not a permanent substance but a constant succession of new moments of fire. He proposes a logical crossroad to determine if flame dies because its cause ceases or because of external environmental pressure.</summary>
<keywords>Francis Bacon, salts, quicksilver, mercury, gunpowder, expansion, nature of flame, fuel, motion, light, physics of fire</keywords>
